Canopy · proof of concept

Checking a Tent

Three plants drifted out of sync with the database in a fortnight, each found by accident. This page asks the question the app never asked, and does not act on the answer.

StatusProof of concept, merged
Date21 September 2026
Commita98c4d8
ScreensSpaces → check contents

01The problem

Nothing in Canopy checks whether the database still matches the tents. In one fortnight three plants were in a different state on the shelf than in the app. Each was found by accident, days or weeks late.

PlantCanopy saidThe tent saidDriftFound by
Sour DieselIn veg, never flippedIn flower since 1 Sep, 3 gallon20 daysA remark about pollinating it
Jack HererIn vegIn flower since 4 Sep10 daysAsking for a clone
SSDD IIIHarvested 30 Aug with its groupStill standing in flower19 daysReading the label

Sour Diesel had been flowering for three weeks. The move was in the grower's written notes the whole time. Canopy never asked whether its record was still true.

This is not a data entry problem. Every screen reports what the database believes. None of them checks it against the tent.

02The main decision

What happens to a plant you cannot find?

Marking it dead is wrong. “I did not see it” and “it is gone” are different claims. A plant can be missed because it is behind a taller one, because two share a pot, because the label faded, or because you were tired. Only the grower can tell that apart from a real loss.

So the check does not change anything. It never sets a status, an end date, or a location. An unticked plant gets a dated note saying it was not found, and appears in a journal entry. That is all. The grower decides what it means later, with the plant in front of them.

The rest of Canopy already works this way: the journal is inert, pollination is recorded and not modelled, capacity is a label and not an alert.

03Options

OptionWhat it doesWhy notVerdict
Do nothingRely on moves being recorded as they happen This is what was already happening. Three drifts in a fortnight, none caught. rejected
Staleness warningsFlag plants not edited in N days Measures record-keeping, not reality. A plant edited last week can still be in the wrong tent.rejected
Confirm-on-sightA tick box on every plant row everywhere Spreads the job across every screen and never finishes. A check only means something against a closed set: this space, now, all of it.rejected
Walk one spaceOne page per space, in walking order, tick what you see Bounded and repeatable. Produces a dated record. Leaves every judgement to the grower. chosen

04Design

Grouped like the tent

Plants are listed by group, because groups sit together physically. Each row shows the label, strain, status and container, which is enough to match a plant to its tag.

Ticking is the fast path

Most of a check is confirming. Ticked rows strike through, so you track what is left rather than what is done. Tick all then unticking the exceptions is usually quicker. The expected count is at the top; a mismatch in the total is itself a finding.

A box for what the app does not know

Sour D was not missing from veg. It was present in the flower tent, which the app knew nothing about. A free-text box records anything on the shelf that is not on the page, and that text goes into the journal entry.

Output is a journal entry

Submitting writes one entry against the space: how many were confirmed out of how many expected, which were not found, and any free text. It is a dated observation, so the journal is the right place for it.

05Result

The veg tent, 35 plants expected.

06What a flagged plant gets

Unticking five plants and submitting produces this and nothing else:

  • Each flagged plant gains a note: Not found in the 2026-09-21 check of Veg Tent. Appended, not overwriting.
  • One journal entry on the space, Checked Veg Tent, recording 30 of 35 confirmed, naming the five, with any free text.
  • The page shows when it was last checked and how it went.

No status changes, no end dates, no moves. A test asserts a flagged plant keeps its status, keeps a null ended_on, and is not killed.

07Limits

  • It does not say where a missing plant went. Sour D would be flagged missing from veg on one walk and reported as unlisted in flower on another. Joining those up is manual. Doing it automatically would be an inference, which this page avoids.
  • "Here but not in Canopy" is free text. It could offer to create the plant; it does not, because a half-known plant entered in a hurry is how records go bad.
  • Nothing prompts a check. No cadence, no reminder.
  • Where several seeds share a pot, one row can stand for more than one plant. That predates this page.
